headline: Philippine Inflation Eases to 6.1%, but Lowest-Income Households Face 8.2%
seoTitle: Philippine Inflation Eases to 6.1% in August 2026 | FMB News
seoDescription: Philippine headline inflation eased to 6.1% in August 2026, while inflation for the bottom 30% income households remained at 8.2%, PSA data show.
deck: Headline inflation slowed for a fourth straight month in August, but official data show the country’s bottom 30% income households continued to experience substantially faster price increases than the national average.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Philippine headline inflation eased to 6.1% in August 2026 from 6.2% in July, the Philippine Statistics Authority reported on September 4. It was the fourth consecutive month of slower headline inflation.

The improvement was modest and did not translate equally across households. Inflation for the bottom 30% income households remained at 8.2% in August, unchanged from July and well above the national headline rate.

The PSA said the national slowdown was mainly influenced by slower price increases in food and non-alcoholic beverages. Core inflation, which excludes selected volatile food and energy items, also eased to 4.1% from 4.2% in July. The national year-to-date average stood at 5.2% through August.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: Inflation measures how quickly consumer prices are rising compared with a year earlier. A lower inflation rate means prices are increasing more slowly; it does not mean that the general price level has fallen.

The gap between the headline figure and the 8.2% rate for the bottom 30% matters because lower-income households spend a larger share of their budgets on essentials. PSA data show that inflation for this income group remained especially elevated outside Metro Manila, where it rose to 8.4% in August from 8.3% in July.

sections.heading: Why this matters to Filipinos
paragraphs: For families already operating on tight budgets, the distinction between slower national inflation and actual household costs is significant. An 8.2% inflation rate for the lowest-income group means the basket of goods and services used to measure their spending was still becoming more expensive at a substantially faster pace than the national average.

The national slowdown is nevertheless relevant for monetary policy, business costs and household expectations. Whether the easing continues will depend on food prices, energy and transport costs, weather disruptions, the peso and external risks that can feed into domestic prices.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch the September inflation reading for evidence that the four-month easing trend is continuing, and whether inflation for lower-income households begins to fall rather than merely hold steady.

Food, fuel, electricity and transport costs remain particularly important to household budgets. Future Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas policy decisions will also depend on incoming inflation and growth data and on external price pressures.

audit.socialCaption: Philippine headline inflation eased to 6.1% in August, but the picture is much tougher for lower-income households: inflation for the bottom 30% remained at 8.2%. The national rate is slowing, but the pressure on essential household budgets remains significantly higher.
verificationNotes: The Philippine Statistics Authority directly confirmed that headline inflation eased to 6.1% in August 2026 from 6.2% in July and that core inflation eased to 4.1%.
A separate PSA release directly confirmed that inflation for the bottom 30% income households remained at 8.2% in August and that the rate outside Metro Manila increased to 8.4%.
GMA News and the Philippine News Agency independently corroborated the 6.1% national inflation reading and the PSA's explanation that slower food-price increases contributed to the easing.
The article distinguishes a lower inflation rate from falling prices; it does not imply that consumer prices declined overall.
Repository search found no matching FMB News article for the August 2026 inflation release before publication.
The hero and social crops are FMB-owned editorial graphics using the approved FMB icon and are explicitly not documentary photographs.
